subject: anatomy
title: Fetal Circulation and Circulatory Changes at Birth

steps.tx: The human **fetal circulation** is anatomically configured to bypass nonventilated, high-resistance fetal lungs and prioritize highly oxygenated placental blood delivery to the rapidly developing brain and myocardium. It utilizes three specialized physiological shunts: the ductus venosus, the foramen ovale, and the ductus arteriosus.
steps.say: The fetal circulation is arranged to bypass high-resistance, fluid-filled lungs and direct oxygen-rich placental blood to the brain and heart. It relies on three vascular shunts: the ductus venosus, the foramen ovale, and the ductus arteriosus.

vis.alt: Fetal circulation pathways, shunts, and adult ligamentous remnants
vis.caption: Fetal circulatory shunts and postpartum vascular transformation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Oxygenated blood returning from the placenta travels via the single left umbilical vein with an oxygen saturation of eighty percent. Arriving at the liver, roughly half of this blood enters the hepatic sinusoids while the remainder bypasses the liver through the **ductus venosus**, flowing straight into the inferior vena cava and reaching the right atrium.
steps.say: Placental blood returns through the left umbilical vein with eighty percent oxygen saturation. Reaching the liver, half flows through hepatic sinusoids while the rest bypasses hepatic tissue through the ductus venosus directly into the inferior vena cava.

nodes.label: Inferior Vena Cava to Right Atrium

steps.tx: Inside the right atrium, the crista dividens of the limbus fossae ovalis directs the well-oxygenated stream from the inferior vena cava across the **foramen ovale** directly into the left atrium. From the left ventricle, this high-oxygen blood enters the ascending aorta to preferentially supply the carotid and coronary arteries nourishing the brain and heart.
steps.say: Within the right atrium, the crista dividens channels the stream from the inferior vena cava across the foramen ovale into the left atrium. This blood enters the ascending aorta to nourish the coronary arteries and developing brain.

left.title: Inferior Vena Cava Stream
points: Guided by valve of IVC (Eustachian valve)
Streams across foramen ovale to left atrium

right.title: Superior Vena Cava Stream
points: Directed across tricuspid into right ventricle
Shunted across ductus arteriosus to lower body

steps.tx: Conversely, deoxygenated blood returning from the fetal upper body via the superior vena cava is directed across the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. The right ventricle pumps this blood into the pulmonary artery, where ninety percent bypasses the high-resistance fetal lungs through the **ductus arteriosus** directly into the descending aorta.
steps.say: Deoxygenated blood from the upper body enters the right ventricle and is ejected into the pulmonary trunk. Ninety percent of this flow bypasses the nonventilated lungs through the ductus arteriosus, dumping directly into the descending aorta.

nodes.label: Descending Aorta to Viscera and Placenta

steps.tx: Dramatic circulatory changes occur at birth triggered by the newborn first breath and cord clamping. Pulmonary aeration expands alveolar capillaries, causing **pulmonary vascular resistance** to plunge dramatically. Blood flow through the pulmonary arteries surges, dramatically augmenting venous return to the left atrium and raising left atrial pressure above right atrial pressure.
steps.say: Sweeping vascular adjustments take place at birth upon the infant first breath and cord clamping. Lung expansion plunges pulmonary vascular resistance, sending massive blood flow through pulmonary veins into the left atrium and raising left atrial pressure.

rows: Rising arterial PaO2 and falling PGE2

steps.tx: A single lipid messenger decides whether a newborn circulation stays fetal or converts. **Prostaglandin E2** keeps the ductus arteriosus open before birth, and its fall after delivery, with rising oxygen, lets the duct close. Clinicians exploit both directions: prostaglandin infusion maintains duct dependent hearts until surgery, while inhibitors close a persistent duct in preterm infants. The same drug class therefore rescues one baby and treats another, depending entirely on the lesion.
steps.say: Prostaglandin E2 holds the ductus arteriosus open before birth. Infusing it rescues duct dependent hearts, while blocking it closes a persistent duct in preterm infants.

vis.alt: Diagram of prostaglandin E2 maintaining patency of the ductus arteriosus in fetal circulation.
vis.caption: Prostaglandin E2 is shown holding the ductus arteriosus open between aorta and pulmonary artery. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The reversal of the interatrial pressure gradient presses the flexible septum primum firmly against the muscular septum secundum, functionally sealing the foramen ovale. The ductus arteriosus constricts rapidly in response to rising arterial oxygen tension and falling circulating **prostaglandin E2** levels, closing functionally within fifteen hours post-delivery.
steps.say: The reversed atrial pressure gradient presses the septum primum against the septum secundum, closing the foramen ovale. The ductus arteriosus constricts rapidly due to rising blood oxygen levels and dropping prostaglandin E2, sealing within fifteen hours.

vis.alt: Ductal smooth muscle contraction and vascular wall remodelling
vis.caption: Arterial remodelling and ligamentous obliteration of fetal shunts. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Over subsequent weeks, fibrous obliteration converts each fetal channel into an anatomical adult ligament: the umbilical vein becomes the **ligamentum teres hepatis**, the ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum, the ductus arteriosus becomes the ligamentum arteriosum, and distal umbilical arteries become the medial umbilical ligaments.
steps.say: Over subsequent weeks, fibrous obliteration converts fetal shunts into adult ligaments: the umbilical vein becomes the ligamentum teres, the ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum, and the ductus arteriosus becomes the ligamentum arteriosum.

steps.tx: Failure of the ductus arteriosus to close produces **patent ductus arteriosus**, characterized by a continuous machinery murmur loudest in the left infraclavicular region and a wide pulse pressure. Coarctation of the aorta typically involves the juxtaductal region near the insertion of the ligamentum arteriosum, presenting with upper extremity hypertension and delayed, diminished femoral pulses.
steps.say: Failure of ductal closure causes patent ductus arteriosus, recognized by a continuous machinery murmur below the left clavicle and bounding pulses. Juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta near the ligamentum arteriosum produces upper body hypertension with weak femoral pulses.

left.title: Patent Ductus Arteriosus
points: Left-to-right shunt from aorta to pulmonary
Treated with indomethacin or surgical ligation
Maintained patent in cyanotic heart disease with PGE1
